answer: Sequential work receipts. An agent earns standing by completing a verified chain of prior tasks whose ordering is checked against a shared kernel of task dependencies. Each new identity must redo a costly serial computation path to enter the grove of eligible workers, since receipts cannot be copied or parallelized. A cipher ties each receipt to the worker's prior output, so forging history means recomputing the whole chain. Attacker cost: hours of serial compute per identity, scaling linearly.
